videos.title: Reactive Streams demand: the publisher sends only what the subscriber asked for
The cook's bookmark: a suspend function becomes a state machine, and one small continuation object keeps its step and its local variables
One burned roast: in the job tree, a failure goes up and stops the siblings, and a cancel only goes down
A thread per connection versus one thread asking a Selector what is ready
Netty's event loop and pipeline: reads flow in, writes flow out, never block
flatMap emits in completion order; concatMap and flatMapSequential keep input order

A cancel only asks: the cook hears it between steps while a loop with no check sorts the whole sack (2,851 ms), suspending cleanup needs NonCancellable to give the jam pan back, and a timeout is a cancel with a timer that a blocking call hears only through runInterruptible

A cold flow is a recipe card: it cooks nothing until someone collects, and each collector cooks it from the top; steps only write on the card, the terminal one cooks, flowOn moves the steps above it, catch handles what falls from above and onCompletion every ending
A Vert.x context runs a verticle's handlers on one event-loop thread, so never block it
Zero-copy with transferTo, then readiness (epoll) versus completion (io_uring)
A source that can't slow down needs a loss policy: buffer keeps a small pile, drop uses a bin, latest keeps the newest, error stops the line, and none of them slows the source

A dispatcher picks the thread: Default is the counter with one cutting board per core, IO the bench by the door for blocking calls, withContext carries one step there and back, and a limitedParallelism view gives the bakery its own 20 seats
The quote service you build, sitting by sitting: a Netty shell, a coroutine fan-out, guards under load, and the earlier lesson behind each part

A burnt dish tells its parent at once, from launch or async alike; a supervisor keeps one burnt tray from spoiling the rest, the handler is the notebook by the oven for failures at the top, and launch(SupervisorJob()) cuts the child out of the tree
publishOn moves everything after it, subscribeOn moves the source wherever it is written (the one nearest the source wins), and a blocking call needs boundedElastic on its own Mono

The menu board and the house bell: a StateFlow keeps one current value, so a busy collector sees only the last choice; a SharedFlow's buffer decides which rings are lost; stateIn shares one cold flow among many screens; and only the kitchen writes, in one step
Assembly only builds a chain of objects; subscribe travels up, request follows, data flows down, and a second subscribe runs it all again
Jetty's acceptor, selectors and one thread pool: a ready socket becomes a task, and the handler's declaration picks the thread that runs it

The hatch between kitchen and dining room: a channel hands each plate to exactly one receiver and its shelf sets the pace, a team of helpers caps the work, select takes whichever answer comes first, and without close the helper waits all night
A course waits for its dishes: launch and async return at once, and coroutineScope returns only when every child it started has finished
A blocked read parks a whole thread, so ten thousand idle connections hold ten thousand threads; readiness lets one thread watch them all
The pen goes down at every suspension: a one-thread view keeps other helpers out only between suspensions, a Mutex holds across them, and runTest skips delays on a virtual clock
An error ends the stream: error operators replace the rest, retry subscribes again from the source (3 retries are 4 attempts), and a timeout turns silence into an error

Two belts, four ways to join them: merge passes items as they arrive, concat starts the next belt after the bell, zip pairs by position and ships nothing when a belt is empty, combineLatest recomputes on every change

Cold plays the recording again for each subscriber; share, replay(1) and cache make it a live show and decide what a latecomer gets, and a multicast sink is a bell your own code rings, one thread at a time

The neighbour's ticket: get() keeps a thread at the fence and drops the cancel, await() suspends and cancels the future, future { } hands Java a ticket tied to our coroutine, and a cold mono { } runs one coroutine per subscriber
A decoder frames bytes that arrive in chunks of any size, writability and auto-read stop a slow client from filling your memory, and a buffer nobody releases never goes back to the pool

Every request arrives on an IO thread; the signature sends it to a worker, keeps it on the event loop, or gives it a virtual thread, and blocking code on the event loop stalls every connection behind it

One request, three providers, one deadline (Kotlin coroutines): start every call together, give each the deadline, let each fail alone, rethrow only your own cancel, and serve the last good quote marked stale

Hedge the slow tail: when Northbank's first call hasn't answered by 80 ms, send one identical call, take the first answer and cancel the other; p99 falls from 600 to 120 ms for 5% more calls, and only safe-to-repeat calls may be hedged

The inspector at the kitchen door: flow { } checks every emit (dinner still on, same context, nothing after a sent-back plate), so a polite try/catch around emit loses the roast; the library's own operators skip the inspector, and take stops the cook with a signed note thrown back through emit

Ten dishes, four burners: flatMapMerge's head cook runs your lambda one dish at a time and only the returned flow gets a burner (1,000 ms, not 300); flatMapConcat makes the outer wait inside emit (800 ms), flatMapMerge runs side by side (400) and flatMapLatest bins the old dish (400)
The cook waits at the table: the collector runs inside emit, so a flow is cold, serves one dish at a time, and with a 100 ms cook and a 300 ms diner the second emit comes at 500 ms, not 200

catch is a net under the cook that asks who threw: an upstream timeout lands in it and becomes crackers, while the diner's dropped plate and the caller's own cancel go past; retry(3) cooks the recipe again from the top, and a backoff rings the bakery at 0, 100, 300 and 700 ms

flowOn(io) builds a wall with a hatch: the reader runs behind it in a second coroutine, a 64-spot shelf lets it get 65 ahead, and the collector and the pantry book never move, which is why withContext around emit is refused; channelFlow lets two cooks share one hatch

A shelf in the hatch: buffer(n) lets the cook get n + 1 dumplings ahead, conflate keeps only the newest reading, side-by-side buffers fuse into one shelf, and collectLatest waits for the cancelled drawing's cleanup

One slate by the house bell for every listener: under DROP_LATEST the slow diary keeper makes the quick waiter lose 4, 5 and 6; the menu board (StateFlow) keeps one slot and skips what a busy reader missed; WhileSubscribed(5_000) keeps one cook going until 5 s after the last diner leaves

A hatch fitted to the old oven probe: callbackFlow registers only when its producer runs, so a reading fired at once is lost; trySend fills a 64-spot shelf (65 of a 200 burst get in), awaitClose takes the hatch down, Java gets a Flux, and advanceTimeBy(100) stops just before a task due at 100
